entwurf.beschreibung: Explore Levi Strauss & Co.'s rise from a 19th‑century dry‑goods shop to the global denim powerhouse, spotlighting key patents, market shifts, and labor challenges.

teile.bildtext: Levi Strauss opens his first shop in San Francisco (1853).
teile.name: Origin
teile.szene: A 19th‑century San Francisco street, cobblestones, a small dry‑goods shop with brass signage. A young Levi Strauss stands beside a wooden counter, greeting customers. Sunlight streams through a large window, casting long shadows. The scene feels bustling yet intimate, reflecting early commerce.
teile.text: A Reno tailor, Jacob Davis, noticed customers’ denim jeans tore in high‑wear areas. He added copper rivets to strengthen pocket corners, a simple fix that saved the fabric. Levi Strauss, a San Francisco dry‑goods shop owner, partnered with Davis in 1873 to secure U.S. patent 139,121. The rivet became the hallmark of the 501 overalls introduced in 1890. During World II the rivets were removed to conserve metal, but watch‑pocket rivets returned later. So what made Levi’s a cultural icon? The durable design turned denim into everyday fashion. Like, share, save.
